preconditions.description: The number of cities (n), roads (m), and queries (q) are within the specified bounds.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= T_i <= 10**9 for T_i in T)
preconditions.description: Each city's building type T_i is a positive integer up to 10^9.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u_i <= 10**9 for u_i in road_crowds)
preconditions.description: Each road's crowd value u_i is a positive integer up to 10^9.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x_i <= n and 1 <= y_i <= n and x_i != y_i for x_i, y_i, _ in roads)
preconditions.description: Each road connects two distinct cities within the valid range.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x_j <= n and 1 <= y_j <= n and 1 <= k_j <= n for x_j, y_j, k_j in queries)
preconditions.description: Each query's start city (x_j), destination city (y_j), and minimum unique building types (k_j) are within valid bounds.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly one line per query.

postconditions.expression: all(answer in [-1] or (1 <= int(answer) <= 10**9) for answer in stdout.splitlines())
postconditions.description: Each answer is either -1 (no valid path) or a positive integer representing the minimum crowd value.

postconditions.expression: all((x_j, y_j, k_j, answer) in [(x, y, k, stdout.splitlines()[i]) for i, (x, y, k) in enumerate(queries)] and (answer == '-1' or (path_exists_with_k_types(x, y, k) and min_crowd_value(x, y, k) == int(answer))))
postconditions.description: For each query (x_j, y_j, k_j), the output is either -1 if no path exists with at least k_j unique building types, or the minimum crowd value of such a path. The path must exist and satisfy the crowd value constraint.
